item.title: [Campaign: new] Intune ending support for Windows MDM-only enrollment CNAME auto-discovery
item.description:
Starting January 15, 2027 , or soon after, Intune will no longer support domain name server (DNS) CNAME-based auto-discovery for Windows MDM-only enrollment scenarios.

Next: 15 Jan 2027.

Open in the Microsoft SOC Brief

item.title: [New] Intune ends CNAME auto-discovery for Windows MDM-only enrollment on 15 January 2027
item.description:
A stale EnterpriseEnrollment CNAME that nobody owns is a record an attacker could point elsewhere; once discovery stops using it, it can be removed.

Intune · Find out whether any Windows MDM-only enrollment still relies on the CNAME, update the enrollment instructions before January, and remove the EnterpriseEnrollment record once nothing uses it.

item.title: [Message Center] MC1509780 Intune ending support for Windows MDM-only enrollment CNAME auto-discovery
item.description:
Starting January 15, 2027, Intune will end support for DNS CNAME auto-discovery in Windows MDM-only enrollment. Organizations using this must have users manually enter the Microsoft enrollment server URL. Existing devices and other enrollment methods remain unaffected. Update enrollment procedures accordingly.

Microsoft Intune · Plan for Change · act by 2027-01-15

item.title: [New] Azure Virtual Desktop multi-session: Intune no longer promises that orphaned device records go after 30 and 60 days; it only attempts deletion after 60 days of inactivity, and that is not guaranteed
item.description:
Deleted session hosts stay in Intune, Entra and the Defender device inventory for an open-ended time instead of a stated 60 days, so stale device objects can keep compliance state and inflate the inventory a SOC hunts across.

Intune · Do not rely on automatic removal: set an Intune device cleanup rule, and delete the Entra and Intune device objects when a host pool is torn down.

item.title: [Learn] Microsoft Intune: Faster Win32 app delivery after Windows enrollment
item.description:

item.title: [Learn] Microsoft Intune: New Apple settings in the Settings Catalog for iOS/iPadOS and macOS
item.description:
Microsoft Intune now includes new Apple Settings Catalog options for supported iOS/iPadOS and macOS devices. You can configure additional controls for areas such as app settings, Apple Intelligence, network and web-content filtering, and the macOS login window by using the same Settings Catalog policy workflow in the Microsoft Intune admin center. For more information, see Create a policy using settings catalog. Applies to: - iOS/iPadOS - macOS

item.title: [New] Remote Help: Microsoft adds a limitation, Windows unattended remote sign-in isn't available for tenants in the Switzerland North datacenter region
item.description:
Unattended control lets a helper reach a physical, corporate-owned Windows device with nobody present. A tenant hosted in Switzerland North that planned on it for kiosk or server-room support does not get it, and Microsoft gives no date for a change.

Intune · If your Intune tenant's data is hosted in the Switzerland North region, keep an attended support path for Windows devices. Other tenants need no action.
